 140: \begin{proposition}[Dyadic boundary functional]
 141: \label{prop:dyadic-boundary-functional}
 142: Let \(0<x<1\), and let \(Q\) be a polynomial with \(Q(0)=1\) and no zero on
 143: the radial segment \([0,x]\).  Use the logarithm germ continued from zero
 144: along that segment and define
 145: \[
 146:  \mathscr B_x(P):=-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log P(x^{2^j})
 147: \]
 148: whenever the series converges.  Then
 149: \begin{equation}\label{eq:dyadic-boundary-coboundary}
 150:  \mathscr B_x\bigl(Q(z^2)\bigr)
 151:  -\mathscr B_x\bigl(Q(z)^2\bigr)=2\log Q(x).
 152: \end{equation}
 153: Hence \(Q(x)=1\) places the non-constant determinant ratio
 154: \(Q(z^2)/Q(z)^2\) in the kernel of this single boundary functional.
 155: \end{proposition}
 156: 
 157: \begin{proof}
 158: Put \(q_j=\log Q(x^{2^j})\).  Since \(q_j=O(x^{2^j})\), both series converge
 159: absolutely, and shifting the first one gives
 160: \[
 161:  -\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}q_{j+1}
 162:  +2\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}q_j=2q_0.
 163: \]
 164: This is \eqref{eq:dyadic-boundary-coboundary}.
 165: \end{proof}
 166: 
 167: The polynomial identity above belongs to a slightly larger class of finite
 168: rational certificates.  The positivity condition in the next statement is
 169: essential: without it, the positive real powers defining the boundary product
 170: need not exist.
 171: 
 172: \begin{proposition}[Positive rational Mahler certificates]
 173: \label{prop:rational-mahler-certificate}
 174: Let \(0<x<1\), let \(H\in\QQ(z)^\times\) satisfy \(H(0)=1\), and assume
 175: that \(H(t)>0\) for \(0\le t\le x\).  Suppose that
 176: \begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-mahler-coboundary}
 177:  H(z)=\delta R(z):=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2}
 178: \end{equation}
 179: for some \(R\in\overline{\QQ}(z)^\times\) with \(R(0)=1\).  Then:
 180: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
 181:  \item the function \(R\) is unique and in fact belongs to
 182:    \(\QQ(z)^\times\);
 183:  \item it has neither a zero nor a pole on \([0,x]\), and \(R(t)>0\) on
 184:    that interval;
 185:  \item the positive real product
 186:    \begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-mahler-product}
 187:     \Pi_x(H):=\prod_{j\ge0}H(x^{2^j})^{2^{-j}}
 188:    \end{equation}
 189:    converges and satisfies
 190:    \begin{equation}\label{eq:rational-mahler-telescope}
 191:     \Pi_x(H)=R(x)^{-2}.
 192:    \end{equation}
 193: \end{enumerate}
 194: Consequently, within the positive rational coboundary class
 195: \[
 196:  \mathscr R_x^+:=\{R\in\QQ(z)^\times:R(0)=1,
 197:                          \ \delta R(t)>0\text{ on }[0,x]\},
 198: \]
 199: one has the exact kernel identity
 200: \begin{equation}\label{eq:positive-rational-certificate-kernel}
 201:  \ker(\Pi_x)\cap\delta\mathscr R_x^+
 202:  =\{\delta R:R\in\mathscr R_x^+,\ R(x)=1\}.
 203: \end{equation}
 204: \end{proposition}
 205: 
 206: \begin{proof}
 207: First, \(\delta\) is injective on rational functions normalized to have value
 208: one at zero.  Indeed, if \(U(0)=1\) and \(U(z^2)=U(z)^2\), write
 209: \(U(z)=1+az^n+O(z^{n+1})\) with \(a\ne0\) and \(n\) least.  The first
 210: non-constant term has degree \(2n\) on the left and degree \(n\) on the
 211: right, a contradiction.  Hence \(U=1\).
 212: 
 213: For every automorphism
 214: \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\QQ}/\QQ)\),
 215: \eqref{eq:rational-mahler-coboundary} gives
 216: \(\delta(\sigma R/R)=1\) and \((\sigma R/R)(0)=1\).  Injectivity gives
 217: \(\sigma R=R\), so \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\); it also proves uniqueness.
 218: 
 219: Let \(v_R(t_0)\) denote the zero or pole order of \(R\) at a real
 220: \(t_0\in(0,x]\).  Since \(H(t_0)\) is finite and non-zero,
 221: \eqref{eq:rational-mahler-coboundary} implies
 222: \[
 223:  v_R(t_0^2)=2v_R(t_0).
 224: \]
 225: If \(v_R(t_0)\ne0\), iteration produces infinitely many distinct zeros or
 226: poles accumulating at zero, contrary to rationality and \(R(0)=1\).
 227: Thus \(R\) has none on \([0,x]\); continuity and \(R(0)=1\) then give
 228: \(R>0\) there.
 229: 
 230: Finally, \(\log H(t)=O(t)\) at zero, so
 231: \eqref{eq:rational-mahler-product} converges absolutely after taking real
 232: logarithms.  Its finite truncations telescope exactly:
 233: \[
 234:  \prod_{j=0}^{N}
 235:  \left(\frac{R(x^{2^{j+1}})}{R(x^{2^j})^2}\right)^{2^{-j}}
 236:  =\frac{R(x^{2^{N+1}})^{2^{-N}}}{R(x)^2}.
 237: \]
 238: The numerator tends to one because \(R(0)=1\), proving
 239: \eqref{eq:rational-mahler-telescope} and then
 240: \eqref{eq:positive-rational-certificate-kernel}.
 241: \end{proof}
 242: 
 243: \begin{remark}[Boundary of the rational certificate]
 244: \label{rem:mahler-kernel-open-interface}
 245: \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} classifies only the intersection of
 246: the boundary kernel with the positive rational coboundary image.  It does not
 247: assert the converse lifting
 248: \[
 249:  H\in\QQ(z)^\times,\quad H>0\text{ on }[0,x],\quad \Pi_x(H)=1
 250:  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad H=\delta R.
 251: \]
 252: The present paper leaves that implication open.  The lifting and purity
 253: results of Adamczewski--Faverjon concern linear regular-singular Mahler
 254: systems \cite{AdamczewskiFaverjon2018MahlerSeveralVariablesII}.  Greuel's
 255: implicit-function theorem requires a strict degree inequality which is not
 256: met by the boundary equation
 257: \(Y(z)^2=H(z)^2Y(z^2)\) in its critical quadratic case
 258: \cite{Greuel2000ImplicitMahler}.  Lam proves transcendence for a particular
 259: weighted Mahler product at non-zero algebraic points, but not multiplicative
 260: relations for arbitrary rational ratios \cite{Lam2025ValuationProducts}.
 261: Thus none of these results supplies the omitted converse, and no such
 262: converse is used below.
 263: 
 264: The realizability restriction does not remove the special-value question.
 265: Indeed, fix \(r\ge2\), an odd integer \(a>0\), and a positive even integer
 266: \(b\), and let \(A\) have diagonal entries \(a\) and off-diagonal entries
 267: \(b\).  Then \(A\) is positive and has Perron root
 268: \(\lambda=a+(r-1)b\).  For any odd integers \(c_i,d_i\) with
 269: \(\lvert c_i\rvert,\lvert d_i\rvert\le a\), the diagonal matrices
 270: \[
 271:  B=\operatorname{diag}(c_1,\ldots,c_r),\qquad
 272:  B'=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_r)
 273: \]
 274: are compatible sign blocks on this same base and satisfy
 275: \(\rad(B),\rad(B')\le a<\lambda\).  Their determinant ratio is
 276: \[
 277:  \frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
 278:  =\frac{\prod_i(1-c_i z)}{\prod_i(1-d_i z)}.
 279: \]
 280: Thus the omitted converse already contains multiplicative-relation questions
 281: for weighted products built from these linear factors; it is not an artifact
 282: of dropping the same-base compatibility or strict-gap hypotheses.
 283: \end{remark}
 284: 
 285: This mechanism is strictly weaker than full \(G\)-cospectrality, equivalently

   1: \section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
   2: 
   3: The theorem of Mohamed and Noorani requires two independent corrections.
   4: Primitivity of the base does not imply Frobenius equidistribution: the
   5: trivial \(C_2\)-cocycle shows that an extension-level
   6: transitivity/aperiodicity condition is necessary.  Under the strict twisted
   7: gap used here, the exponent is \(|C|/|G|\).  At the constant level, the
   8: Frobenius-class product fixes the primitive label \(g_\gamma\), whereas the
   9: periodic Artin logarithm replaces it by \(g_\gamma^r\) on the \(r\)-fold
  10: traversal.  The correct coordinate is therefore \(F_\rho\), with the
  11: finite-determinant formula in \eqref{eq:perron-fixed-determinant}; the strict-gap
  12: \(S_3\) sign channel proves that it cannot generally be replaced by
  13: \(L_\rho\).
  14: 
  15: The discrepancy is universal at the identity class, not confined to the
  16: \(S_3\) witness.  The quotient-cover factor in
  17: \eqref{eq:identity-class-universal-error} is strictly greater than one for
  18: every non-trivial strict-gap extension and records precisely the primitive
  19: orbits whose lifts close only after repeated traversal.  After the constant is
  20: corrected, \eqref{eq:harmonic-renormalized-product} separates the universal
  21: harmonic factor from an exponentially small system-dependent remainder.
  22: 
  23: The vector of corrected constants is nevertheless not an inverse invariant
  24: of the primitive class profile.  The fixed-graph \(C_2\) pair in
  25: \Cref{thm:c2-boundary-collision} has different length-one data but identical
  26: constants, because the dyadic boundary functional annihilates a non-trivial
  27: determinant coboundary at the Perron point.  This collision is strictly weaker
  28: than full \(G\)-cospectrality.  The positive rational coboundary part of this
  29: kernel has the unique certificate in
  30: \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate}; the converse classification of all
  31: isolated numerical collisions is not asserted.  Retaining an analytic radial profile
  32: on a set with an interior accumulation point removes the loss by
  33: \Cref{thm:radial-profile-recovery}; no claim of minimality is attached to that
  34: analytic enhancement.
  35: 
  36: For a homogeneous union of classes, the downstream constant is
  37: \eqref{eq:homogeneous-union-constant}.  The M\"obius transform used to obtain
  38: it is standard necklace/Witt calculus; the paper-specific point is its use on
  39: the fixed-label coordinate before Adams powering.  The appendices record only
  40: the determinant-derived radial convention and established periodic-data and
  41: gain-graph translations needed to fix the scope of the main result.

+def critical_mahler_normalization_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify that the weighted product is F(x)^2, rather than F(x)."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    x = sp.Rational(1, 3)
+    h = (1 - z) / (1 + z)
+    f = 1 - z
+    symbolic = all(
+        (
+            sp.cancel(f**2 - h * f.subs(z, z**2)) == 0,
+            f.subs(z, x) == sp.Rational(2, 3),
+            f.subs(z, x) ** 2 == sp.Rational(4, 9),
+            f.subs(z, x) != f.subs(z, x) ** 2,
+        )
+    )
+    if not symbolic:
+        return False
+
+    with mp.workdps(80):
+        real_x = mp.mpf(1) / 3
+        logarithmic_product = mp.fsum(
+            mp.power(2, -nu)
+            * mp.log((1 - real_x ** (2**nu)) / (1 + real_x ** (2**nu)))
+            for nu in range(12)
+        )
+        product_value = mp.exp(logarithmic_product)
+        return (
+            abs(product_value - mp.mpf(4) / 9) < mp.mpf("1e-70")
+            and abs(product_value - (1 - real_x)) > mp.mpf("1e-2")
+        )
+
+
+def _critical_mahler_coefficients(order: int) -> tuple[sp.Integer, ...]:
+    """Solve F^2=((1-z)/(1-3z))F(z^2) coefficient by coefficient."""
+    h_coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)] + [
+        2 * sp.Integer(3) ** (degree - 1) for degree in range(1, order + 1)
+    ]
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+    for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+        known_square = sum(
+            coefficients[index] * coefficients[degree - index]
+            for index in range(1, degree)
+        )
+        right_hand_side = sum(
+            h_coefficients[degree - 2 * index] * coefficients[index]
+            for index in range(degree // 2 + 1)
+        )
+        coefficients.append(sp.simplify((right_hand_side - known_square) / 2))
+    return tuple(coefficients)
+
+
+def critical_mahler_integrality_matches(order: int = 24) -> bool:
+    """Check determinant parity, integral recursion, and the truncated equation."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(order)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    residual = sp.series(
+        f**2 - (p_zero / p_one) * f.subs(z, z**2), z, 0, order + 1
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(p_zero - p_one, z).all_coeffs()[-1] % 2 == 0,
+            all(coefficient.is_Integer for coefficient in coefficients),
+            sp.expand(residual) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def critical_zero_estimate_pullback_matches() -> bool:
+    """Check the cleared pullback identity and its two bidegree bounds."""
+    z, y = sp.symbols("z y")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    q = y**2 + z * y + z + 1
+    d = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(z)
+    n = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(y)
+    eta = max(sp.degree(p_zero, z), sp.degree(p_one, z))
+    pullback = sp.cancel(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: p_one * y**2 / p_zero}, simultaneous=True)
+    )
+    pullback = sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).as_expr()
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(18)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    evaluated_pullback = sp.series(pullback.subs(y, f), z, 0, 19).removeO()
+    expected = sp.series(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: f.subs(z, z**2)}, simultaneous=True),
+        z,
+        0,
+        19,
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(q, z, y).is_irreducible,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(y) <= 2 * n,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(z) <= 2 * d + eta * n,
+            sp.expand(evaluated_pullback - expected) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def rational_mahler_saturation_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify normalized saturation identities in exact rational examples."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    examples = (
+        ((1 - z) ** 2 * (1 + 2 * z) / ((1 - 3 * z) * (1 + z) ** 3), 2),
+        ((1 + z + z**2) / ((1 - 2 * z) ** 2 * (1 + 3 * z)), 3),
+        ((1 - 4 * z) * (1 + z) ** 2 / (1 + 2 * z**2), 5),
+    )
+    for rational_r, exponent in examples:
+        rational_r = sp.cancel(rational_r)
+        h = sp.cancel(rational_r.subs(z, z**2) / rational_r**2)
+        q = sp.cancel(rational_r**exponent)
+        delta_q = sp.cancel(q.subs(z, z**2) / q**2)
+        numerator, denominator = sp.fraction(q)
+        factor_exponents = [
+            multiplicity
+            for polynomial in (numerator, denominator)
+            for _factor, multiplicity in sp.factor_list(polynomial)[1]
+        ]
+        if not all(
+            (
+                rational_r.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                h.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                q.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                sp.cancel(h**exponent - delta_q) == 0,
+                all(multiplicity % exponent == 0 for multiplicity in factor_exponents),
+            )
+        ):
+            return False
+    return True
+

                  ON A PROBLEM OF MAHLER FOR TRANSCENDENCY
                                      OF FUNCTION VALUES

                                                         KUMIKO NISfflOKA

                                                  (Received 28 May 1981; revised 7 January 1982)
                                                       Communicated by A. J. van der Poorten

                                                                            Abstract
               A transcendence theorem is proved for functions satisfying functional equations of the shape
               P(z, /(z), f(zp)) = 0, where P is a polynomial and p > 2 is an integer.
                1980 Mathematics subject classification (Amer. Math. Soc): 10 F 35

                                                              1. Introduction

            In a sequence of three papers, K. Mahler (1929, 1930a, 1930b) discussed the
            arithmetic properties of functions in several complex variables satisfying a certain
             type of functional equation. Mahler (1969) gave a summary of his earlier work
            and proposed three problems connected with it. Two of the three problems have
            been studied by K. K. Kubota, J. H. Loxton, A. J. van der Poorten and D. W.
            Masser. (An account of the progress up to 1977 is given in Loxton and van der
            Poorten (1977).) The present investigation is concerned with the remaining
            problem. Specifically, this problem asks for the transcendency at algebraic points
            of functions / ( z ) satisfying algebraic functional equations of the form
            P(z, f(z), f(zp)) = 0, where P is a polynomial and/? > 2 is an integer. The same
            question can be asked for functions of several complex variables, with an
            appropriate generalization of the transformation z -* zp. We shall consider only
            functions of one variable, but we generalize the basic transformation z -> zp in a
            different way, as follows.

+            sp.Poly(p_zero - p_one, z).all_coeffs()[-1] % 2 == 0,
+            all(coefficient.is_Integer for coefficient in coefficients),
+            sp.expand(residual) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def critical_zero_estimate_pullback_matches() -> bool:
+    """Check the cleared pullback identity and its two bidegree bounds."""
+    z, y = sp.symbols("z y")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    q = y**2 + z * y + z + 1
+    d = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(z)
+    n = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(y)
+    eta = max(sp.degree(p_zero, z), sp.degree(p_one, z))
+    pullback = sp.cancel(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: p_one * y**2 / p_zero}, simultaneous=True)
+    )
+    pullback = sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).as_expr()
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(18)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    evaluated_pullback = sp.series(pullback.subs(y, f), z, 0, 19).removeO()
+    expected = sp.series(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: f.subs(z, z**2)}, simultaneous=True),
+        z,
+        0,
+        19,
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(q, z, y).is_irreducible,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(y) <= 2 * n,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(z) <= 2 * d + eta * n,
+            sp.expand(evaluated_pullback - expected) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def rational_mahler_saturation_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify normalized saturation identities in exact rational examples."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    examples = (
+        ((1 - z) ** 2 * (1 + 2 * z) / ((1 - 3 * z) * (1 + z) ** 3), 2),
+        ((1 + z + z**2) / ((1 - 2 * z) ** 2 * (1 + 3 * z)), 3),
+        ((1 - 4 * z) * (1 + z) ** 2 / (1 + 2 * z**2), 5),
+    )
+    for rational_r, exponent in examples:
+        rational_r = sp.cancel(rational_r)
+        h = sp.cancel(rational_r.subs(z, z**2) / rational_r**2)
+        q = sp.cancel(rational_r**exponent)
+        delta_q = sp.cancel(q.subs(z, z**2) / q**2)
+        numerator, denominator = sp.fraction(q)
+        factor_exponents = [
+            multiplicity
+            for polynomial in (numerator, denominator)
+            for _factor, multiplicity in sp.factor_list(polynomial)[1]
+        ]
+        if not all(
+            (
+                rational_r.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                h.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                q.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                sp.cancel(h**exponent - delta_q) == 0,
+                all(multiplicity % exponent == 0 for multiplicity in factor_exponents),
+            )
+        ):
+            return False
+    return True
+

+def critical_mahler_normalization_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify that the weighted product is F(x)^2, rather than F(x)."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    x = sp.Rational(1, 3)
+    h = (1 - z) / (1 + z)
+    f = 1 - z
+    symbolic = all(
+        (
+            sp.cancel(f**2 - h * f.subs(z, z**2)) == 0,
+            f.subs(z, x) == sp.Rational(2, 3),
+            f.subs(z, x) ** 2 == sp.Rational(4, 9),
+            f.subs(z, x) != f.subs(z, x) ** 2,
+        )
+    )
+    if not symbolic:
+        return False
+
+    with mp.workdps(80):
+        real_x = mp.mpf(1) / 3
+        logarithmic_product = mp.fsum(
+            mp.power(2, -nu)
+            * mp.log((1 - real_x ** (2**nu)) / (1 + real_x ** (2**nu)))
+            for nu in range(12)
+        )
+        product_value = mp.exp(logarithmic_product)
+        return (
+            abs(product_value - mp.mpf(4) / 9) < mp.mpf("1e-70")
+            and abs(product_value - (1 - real_x)) > mp.mpf("1e-2")
+        )
+
+
+def _critical_mahler_coefficients(order: int) -> tuple[sp.Integer, ...]:
+    """Solve F^2=((1-z)/(1-3z))F(z^2) coefficient by coefficient."""
+    h_coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)] + [
+        2 * sp.Integer(3) ** (degree - 1) for degree in range(1, order + 1)
+    ]
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+    for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+        known_square = sum(
+            coefficients[index] * coefficients[degree - index]
+            for index in range(1, degree)
+        )
+        right_hand_side = sum(
+            h_coefficients[degree - 2 * index] * coefficients[index]
+            for index in range(degree // 2 + 1)
+        )
+        coefficients.append(sp.simplify((right_hand_side - known_square) / 2))
+    return tuple(coefficients)
+
+
+def critical_mahler_integrality_matches(order: int = 24) -> bool:
+    """Check determinant parity, integral recursion, and the truncated equation."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(order)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    residual = sp.series(
+        f**2 - (p_zero / p_one) * f.subs(z, z**2), z, 0, order + 1
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(p_zero - p_one, z).all_coeffs()[-1] % 2 == 0,
+            all(coefficient.is_Integer for coefficient in coefficients),
+            sp.expand(residual) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+

+            sp.cancel(f**2 - h * f.subs(z, z**2)) == 0,
+            f.subs(z, x) == sp.Rational(2, 3),
+            f.subs(z, x) ** 2 == sp.Rational(4, 9),
+            f.subs(z, x) != f.subs(z, x) ** 2,
+        )
+    )
+    if not symbolic:
+        return False
+
+    with mp.workdps(80):
+        real_x = mp.mpf(1) / 3
+        logarithmic_product = mp.fsum(
+            mp.power(2, -nu)
+            * mp.log((1 - real_x ** (2**nu)) / (1 + real_x ** (2**nu)))
+            for nu in range(12)
+        )
+        product_value = mp.exp(logarithmic_product)
+        return (
+            abs(product_value - mp.mpf(4) / 9) < mp.mpf("1e-70")
+            and abs(product_value - (1 - real_x)) > mp.mpf("1e-2")
+        )
+
+
+def _critical_mahler_coefficients(order: int) -> tuple[sp.Integer, ...]:
+    """Solve F^2=((1-z)/(1-3z))F(z^2) coefficient by coefficient."""
+    h_coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)] + [
+        2 * sp.Integer(3) ** (degree - 1) for degree in range(1, order + 1)
+    ]
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+    for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+        known_square = sum(
+            coefficients[index] * coefficients[degree - index]
+            for index in range(1, degree)
+        )
+        right_hand_side = sum(
+            h_coefficients[degree - 2 * index] * coefficients[index]
+            for index in range(degree // 2 + 1)
+        )
+        coefficients.append(sp.simplify((right_hand_side - known_square) / 2))
+    return tuple(coefficients)
+
+
+def critical_mahler_integrality_matches(order: int = 24) -> bool:
+    """Check determinant parity, integral recursion, and the truncated equation."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(order)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    residual = sp.series(
+        f**2 - (p_zero / p_one) * f.subs(z, z**2), z, 0, order + 1
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(p_zero - p_one, z).all_coeffs()[-1] % 2 == 0,
+            all(coefficient.is_Integer for coefficient in coefficients),
+            sp.expand(residual) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def critical_zero_estimate_pullback_matches() -> bool:
+    """Check the cleared pullback identity and its two bidegree bounds."""
+    z, y = sp.symbols("z y")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    q = y**2 + z * y + z + 1
+    d = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(z)
+    n = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(y)
+    eta = max(sp.degree(p_zero, z), sp.degree(p_one, z))
+    pullback = sp.cancel(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: p_one * y**2 / p_zero}, simultaneous=True)
+    )
+    pullback = sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).as_expr()
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(18)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    evaluated_pullback = sp.series(pullback.subs(y, f), z, 0, 19).removeO()
+    expected = sp.series(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: f.subs(z, z**2)}, simultaneous=True),
+        z,
+        0,
+        19,
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(q, z, y).is_irreducible,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(y) <= 2 * n,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(z) <= 2 * d + eta * n,
+            sp.expand(evaluated_pullback - expected) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def rational_mahler_saturation_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify normalized saturation identities in exact rational examples."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    examples = (
+        ((1 - z) ** 2 * (1 + 2 * z) / ((1 - 3 * z) * (1 + z) ** 3), 2),
+        ((1 + z + z**2) / ((1 - 2 * z) ** 2 * (1 + 3 * z)), 3),
+        ((1 - 4 * z) * (1 + z) ** 2 / (1 + 2 * z**2), 5),
+    )
+    for rational_r, exponent in examples:
+        rational_r = sp.cancel(rational_r)
+        h = sp.cancel(rational_r.subs(z, z**2) / rational_r**2)
+        q = sp.cancel(rational_r**exponent)
+        delta_q = sp.cancel(q.subs(z, z**2) / q**2)
+        numerator, denominator = sp.fraction(q)
+        factor_exponents = [
+            multiplicity
+            for polynomial in (numerator, denominator)
+            for _factor, multiplicity in sp.factor_list(polynomial)[1]
+        ]
+        if not all(
+            (
+                rational_r.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                h.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                q.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                sp.cancel(h**exponent - delta_q) == 0,
+                all(multiplicity % exponent == 0 for multiplicity in factor_exponents),
+            )
+        ):
+            return False
+    return True
+

+            sp.cancel(f**2 - h * f.subs(z, z**2)) == 0,
+            f.subs(z, x) == sp.Rational(2, 3),
+            f.subs(z, x) ** 2 == sp.Rational(4, 9),
+            f.subs(z, x) != f.subs(z, x) ** 2,
+        )
+    )
+    if not symbolic:
+        return False
+
+    with mp.workdps(80):
+        real_x = mp.mpf(1) / 3
+        logarithmic_product = mp.fsum(
+            mp.power(2, -nu)
+            * mp.log((1 - real_x ** (2**nu)) / (1 + real_x ** (2**nu)))
+            for nu in range(12)
+        )
+        product_value = mp.exp(logarithmic_product)
+        return (
+            abs(product_value - mp.mpf(4) / 9) < mp.mpf("1e-70")
+            and abs(product_value - (1 - real_x)) > mp.mpf("1e-2")
+        )
+
+
+def _critical_mahler_coefficients(order: int) -> tuple[sp.Integer, ...]:
+    """Solve F^2=((1-z)/(1-3z))F(z^2) coefficient by coefficient."""
+    h_coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)] + [
+        2 * sp.Integer(3) ** (degree - 1) for degree in range(1, order + 1)
+    ]
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+    for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+        known_square = sum(
+            coefficients[index] * coefficients[degree - index]
+            for index in range(1, degree)
+        )
+        right_hand_side = sum(
+            h_coefficients[degree - 2 * index] * coefficients[index]
+            for index in range(degree // 2 + 1)
+        )
+        coefficients.append(sp.simplify((right_hand_side - known_square) / 2))
+    return tuple(coefficients)
+
+
+def critical_mahler_integrality_matches(order: int = 24) -> bool:
+    """Check determinant parity, integral recursion, and the truncated equation."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(order)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    residual = sp.series(
+        f**2 - (p_zero / p_one) * f.subs(z, z**2), z, 0, order + 1
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(p_zero - p_one, z).all_coeffs()[-1] % 2 == 0,
+            all(coefficient.is_Integer for coefficient in coefficients),
+            sp.expand(residual) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def critical_zero_estimate_pullback_matches() -> bool:
+    """Check the cleared pullback identity and its two bidegree bounds."""
+    z, y = sp.symbols("z y")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    q = y**2 + z * y + z + 1
+    d = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(z)
+    n = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(y)
+    eta = max(sp.degree(p_zero, z), sp.degree(p_one, z))
+    pullback = sp.cancel(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: p_one * y**2 / p_zero}, simultaneous=True)
+    )
+    pullback = sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).as_expr()
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(18)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    evaluated_pullback = sp.series(pullback.subs(y, f), z, 0, 19).removeO()
+    expected = sp.series(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: f.subs(z, z**2)}, simultaneous=True),
+        z,
+        0,
+        19,
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(q, z, y).is_irreducible,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(y) <= 2 * n,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(z) <= 2 * d + eta * n,
+            sp.expand(evaluated_pullback - expected) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def rational_mahler_saturation_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify normalized saturation identities in exact rational examples."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    examples = (
+        ((1 - z) ** 2 * (1 + 2 * z) / ((1 - 3 * z) * (1 + z) ** 3), 2),
+        ((1 + z + z**2) / ((1 - 2 * z) ** 2 * (1 + 3 * z)), 3),
+        ((1 - 4 * z) * (1 + z) ** 2 / (1 + 2 * z**2), 5),
+    )
+    for rational_r, exponent in examples:
+        rational_r = sp.cancel(rational_r)
+        h = sp.cancel(rational_r.subs(z, z**2) / rational_r**2)
+        q = sp.cancel(rational_r**exponent)
+        delta_q = sp.cancel(q.subs(z, z**2) / q**2)
+        numerator, denominator = sp.fraction(q)
+        factor_exponents = [
+            multiplicity
+            for polynomial in (numerator, denominator)
+            for _factor, multiplicity in sp.factor_list(polynomial)[1]
+        ]
+        if not all(
+            (
+                rational_r.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                h.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                q.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                sp.cancel(h**exponent - delta_q) == 0,
+                all(multiplicity % exponent == 0 for multiplicity in factor_exponents),
+            )
+        ):
+            return False
+    return True
+

+def critical_mahler_normalization_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify that the weighted product is F(x)^2, rather than F(x)."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    x = sp.Rational(1, 3)
+    h = (1 - z) / (1 + z)
+    f = 1 - z
+    symbolic = all(
+        (
+            sp.cancel(f**2 - h * f.subs(z, z**2)) == 0,
+            f.subs(z, x) == sp.Rational(2, 3),
+            f.subs(z, x) ** 2 == sp.Rational(4, 9),
+            f.subs(z, x) != f.subs(z, x) ** 2,
+        )
+    )
+    if not symbolic:
+        return False
+
+    with mp.workdps(80):
+        real_x = mp.mpf(1) / 3
+        logarithmic_product = mp.fsum(
+            mp.power(2, -nu)
+            * mp.log((1 - real_x ** (2**nu)) / (1 + real_x ** (2**nu)))
+            for nu in range(12)
+        )
+        product_value = mp.exp(logarithmic_product)
+        return (
+            abs(product_value - mp.mpf(4) / 9) < mp.mpf("1e-70")
+            and abs(product_value - (1 - real_x)) > mp.mpf("1e-2")
+        )
+
+
+def _critical_mahler_coefficients(order: int) -> tuple[sp.Integer, ...]:
+    """Solve F^2=((1-z)/(1-3z))F(z^2) coefficient by coefficient."""
+    h_coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)] + [
+        2 * sp.Integer(3) ** (degree - 1) for degree in range(1, order + 1)
+    ]
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+    for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+        known_square = sum(
+            coefficients[index] * coefficients[degree - index]
+            for index in range(1, degree)
+        )
+        right_hand_side = sum(
+            h_coefficients[degree - 2 * index] * coefficients[index]
+            for index in range(degree // 2 + 1)
+        )
+        coefficients.append(sp.simplify((right_hand_side - known_square) / 2))
+    return tuple(coefficients)
+
+
+def critical_mahler_integrality_matches(order: int = 24) -> bool:
+    """Check determinant parity, integral recursion, and the truncated equation."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(order)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    residual = sp.series(
+        f**2 - (p_zero / p_one) * f.subs(z, z**2), z, 0, order + 1
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(p_zero - p_one, z).all_coeffs()[-1] % 2 == 0,
+            all(coefficient.is_Integer for coefficient in coefficients),
+            sp.expand(residual) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def critical_zero_estimate_pullback_matches() -> bool:
+    """Check the cleared pullback identity and its two bidegree bounds."""
+    z, y = sp.symbols("z y")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    q = y**2 + z * y + z + 1
+    d = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(z)
+    n = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(y)
+    eta = max(sp.degree(p_zero, z), sp.degree(p_one, z))
+    pullback = sp.cancel(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: p_one * y**2 / p_zero}, simultaneous=True)
+    )
+    pullback = sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).as_expr()
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(18)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    evaluated_pullback = sp.series(pullback.subs(y, f), z, 0, 19).removeO()
+    expected = sp.series(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: f.subs(z, z**2)}, simultaneous=True),
+        z,
+        0,
+        19,
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(q, z, y).is_irreducible,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(y) <= 2 * n,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(z) <= 2 * d + eta * n,
+            sp.expand(evaluated_pullback - expected) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def rational_mahler_saturation_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify normalized saturation identities in exact rational examples."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    examples = (
+        ((1 - z) ** 2 * (1 + 2 * z) / ((1 - 3 * z) * (1 + z) ** 3), 2),
+        ((1 + z + z**2) / ((1 - 2 * z) ** 2 * (1 + 3 * z)), 3),
+        ((1 - 4 * z) * (1 + z) ** 2 / (1 + 2 * z**2), 5),
+    )
+    for rational_r, exponent in examples:
+        rational_r = sp.cancel(rational_r)
+        h = sp.cancel(rational_r.subs(z, z**2) / rational_r**2)
+        q = sp.cancel(rational_r**exponent)
+        delta_q = sp.cancel(q.subs(z, z**2) / q**2)
+        numerator, denominator = sp.fraction(q)
+        factor_exponents = [
+            multiplicity
+            for polynomial in (numerator, denominator)
+            for _factor, multiplicity in sp.factor_list(polynomial)[1]
+        ]
+        if not all(
+            (
+                rational_r.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                h.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                q.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                sp.cancel(h**exponent - delta_q) == 0,
+                all(multiplicity % exponent == 0 for multiplicity in factor_exponents),
+            )
+        ):
+            return False
+    return True

+\begin{lemma}[Critical quadratic zero estimate]

+\(\sum_i e_id_i\le D\) and \(\sum_i e_in_i\le N\); therefore
+\(\sum_i e_id_in_i\le DN\) and
+\(\sum_i e_in_i^2\le N^2\).  Summing the factor bounds proves
+\eqref{eq:critical-mahler-zero-bound}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Normalized saturation of rational coboundaries]
+\label{lem:rational-mahler-saturation}
+Let \(H,Q\in\QQ(z)^\times\) satisfy \(H(0)=Q(0)=1\).  If, for some
+integer \(m\ge1\),
+\[
+ H^m=\delta Q=\frac{Q(z^2)}{Q(z)^2},
+\]
+then there is an \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\), with \(R(0)=1\), such that
+\(H=\delta R\).
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For \(a\in\overline{\QQ}^\times\), let \(h(a)\) and \(q(a)\) denote the
+coefficients of \([a]\) in the divisors of \(H\) and \(Q\), respectively.
+Taking divisors gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:saturation-divisor-recurrence}
+ mh(a)=q(a^2)-2q(a),
+ \qquad q(a^2)\equiv2q(a)\pmod m.
+\end{equation}
+Fix \(a\ne0,\infty\).  For sufficiently large \(N\), among the
+\(2^N\)-th roots of \(a\) choose \(b_N\) outside the finite support of
+\(\operatorname{div}Q\).  Iterating the congruence along the chain from
+\(b_N\) to \(a\) gives \(q(a)\equiv2^Nq(b_N)\equiv0\pmod m\).
+The coefficient at zero is zero because \(Q(0)=1\), and the degree-zero
+condition on a principal divisor gives the same divisibility at infinity.
+Thus \(\operatorname{div}Q=mD\).
+
+The divisor \(D\) is Galois invariant and has degree zero.  Since
+\(\operatorname{Pic}^0(\mathbb P^1_{\QQ})=0\), choose
+\(S\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with \(\operatorname{div}S=D\), normalized by
+\(S(0)=1\).  Then \(Q/S^m\) is constant, and evaluation at zero gives
+\(Q=S^m\).  It follows that \((H/\delta S)^m=1\).  This rational function is
+constant and has value one at zero, so \(H=\delta S\); take \(R=S\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{proposition}[Algebraic critical products are rational coboundaries]
+\label{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}
+Let \(H\in\QQ(z)^\times\), \(H(0)=1\), and suppose that
+\(F\in1+z\QQ[[z]]\) is algebraic over \(\CC(z)\) and satisfies
+\(F(z)^2=H(z)F(z^2)\).  Then \(H=\delta R\) for a unique
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with \(R(0)=1\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put \(G=zF'/F\).  Logarithmic differentiation gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:log-derivative-mahler}
+ G(z)=G(z^2)+\frac z2\frac{H'(z)}{H(z)}.
+\end{equation}
+If the rational inhomogeneous term is non-zero, the equations at \(z\) and
+\(z^2\) eliminate it to give a homogeneous scalar (2)-Mahler equation for
+\(G\); if it is zero, \eqref{eq:log-derivative-mahler} and \(G(0)=0\) give
+\(G=0\).  Since algebraic functions are D-finite, B\'ezivin's theorem that a
+D-finite Mahler function is rational
+\cite[Theorem~1]{BellCoonsRowland2013MahlerDichotomy} yields
+\(G\in\CC(z)\), and its rational Taylor coefficients give
+\(G\in\QQ(z)\).
+
+All analytic branches of the algebraic function \(F\) have the same rational
+logarithmic derivative, so their pairwise quotients are constants.  Finite
+monodromy therefore gives an \(m\ge1\) for which
+\(T=F^m\) is single-valued, hence \(T\in\CC(z)^\times\).  Its Taylor
+coefficients give \(T\in\QQ(z)^\times\), and \(T(0)=1\).  Raising the
+functional equation to the (m)-th power gives
+\[
+ H^m=\frac{T(z)^2}{T(z^2)}=\delta(T^{-1}).
+\]
+Apply \Cref{lem:rational-mahler-saturation}, and then use the normalized
+injectivity proved in \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} for uniqueness.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Strict-gap determinant boundary lifting]
+\label{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting}
+Let \(A\) be a primitive non-negative integer matrix with Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\).  Let \(B,B'\) be integer matrices
+of the same size such that, entrywise,
+\[
+ \abs{B_{ij}},\abs{B'_{ij}}\le A_{ij},
+ \qquad B_{ij}\equiv B'_{ij}\equiv A_{ij}\pmod2,
+\]
+and suppose that \(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\).  Set
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}.
+\]
+Then the following are equivalent:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
+ \item \(\Pi_x(H)=1\);
+ \item there is a unique \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
+ \[
+  R(0)=R(x)=1,
+  \qquad H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2}.
+ \]
+\end{enumerate}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The strict gaps imply that both determinant polynomials are non-zero on a disk
+\(\abs z<r\) for some \(x<r<1\).  They are positive on \([0,x]\), because
+they are real, non-zero there, and equal one at zero.  Hence (H>0) on that
+interval.  Define (F) by \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-product}.  By
+\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}, it is analytic on \(\abs z<r\), has
+integer coefficients, and satisfies \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-equation}.
+Crucially, the product normalization is
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
+ F(x)^2=\Pi_x(H),
+\end{equation}
+not (F(x)=\Pi_x(H)).
+
+We apply Nishioka's special-value theorem
+\cite[Theorem, p.~387]{Nishioka1982MahlerFunctionValues} to the reduced form
+of
+\[
+ P_0(z)F(z^2)-P_1(z)F(z)^2=0.
+\]
+In her notation one may take (p=2), (N=0), (n=1), (m=2),
+(M=2), (U=1), and coefficient-growth exponent (L=1).  The required
+numerical inequality is (M(p+N)n^2=4<2^{2+1/L}=8).  The integer
+coefficients and analyticity of (F) give the required linear coefficient
+height bound, while the strict gaps ensure that the reduced coefficient
+polynomials do not vanish anywhere on the orbit (x,x^2,x^4,\ldots).
+Consequently, if (F) were transcendental over \(\CC(z)\), then (F(x))
+would be transcendental.
+
+Assume (i).  Positivity and \eqref{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
+give (F(x)=1), so the cited theorem forces (F) to be algebraic.  By
+\Cref{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}, (H=\delta R) for the unique
+normalized rational (R).  Now
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} gives
+(1=\Pi_x(H)=R(x)^{-2}) and (R(x)>0), hence (R(x)=1).  This proves (ii).
+Conversely, (ii) and \eqref{eq:rational-mahler-telescope} give (i), and the
+same proposition gives uniqueness.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Scope of the lifting theorem]
+The determinant parity in \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} is essential
+to the integrality step, so the theorem does not assert the converse for an
+arbitrary positive rational (H).  Its realizable class is nevertheless broad.
+Fix (r\ge2), an odd (a>0), and a positive even (b), and let (A) have
+diagonal entries (a) and off-diagonal entries (b).  Then
+\(\lambda=a+(r-1)b\).  Any diagonal (B=\operatorname{diag}(c_i)) and
+(B'=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)), with odd
+\(\abs{c_i},\abs{d_i}\le a\), satisfies the same-base compatibility and
+strict gaps, and realizes
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{\prod_i(1-c_i z)}{\prod_i(1-d_i z)}.
+\]
 \end{remark}
 
 This mechanism is strictly weaker than full \(G\)-cospectrality, equivalently

+def critical_mahler_normalization_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify that the weighted product is F(x)^2, rather than F(x)."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    x = sp.Rational(1, 3)
+    h = (1 - z) / (1 + z)
+    f = 1 - z
+    symbolic = all(
+        (
+            sp.cancel(f**2 - h * f.subs(z, z**2)) == 0,
+            f.subs(z, x) == sp.Rational(2, 3),
+            f.subs(z, x) ** 2 == sp.Rational(4, 9),
+            f.subs(z, x) != f.subs(z, x) ** 2,
+        )
+    )
+    if not symbolic:
+        return False
+
+    with mp.workdps(80):
+        real_x = mp.mpf(1) / 3
+        logarithmic_product = mp.fsum(
+            mp.power(2, -nu)
+            * mp.log((1 - real_x ** (2**nu)) / (1 + real_x ** (2**nu)))
+            for nu in range(12)
+        )
+        product_value = mp.exp(logarithmic_product)
+        return (
+            abs(product_value - mp.mpf(4) / 9) < mp.mpf("1e-70")
+            and abs(product_value - (1 - real_x)) > mp.mpf("1e-2")
+        )
+
+
+def _critical_mahler_coefficients(order: int) -> tuple[sp.Integer, ...]:
+    """Solve F^2=((1-z)/(1-3z))F(z^2) coefficient by coefficient."""
+    h_coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)] + [
+        2 * sp.Integer(3) ** (degree - 1) for degree in range(1, order + 1)
+    ]
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+    for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+        known_square = sum(
+            coefficients[index] * coefficients[degree - index]
+            for index in range(1, degree)
+        )
+        right_hand_side = sum(
+            h_coefficients[degree - 2 * index] * coefficients[index]
+            for index in range(degree // 2 + 1)
+        )
+        coefficients.append(sp.simplify((right_hand_side - known_square) / 2))
+    return tuple(coefficients)
+
+
+def critical_mahler_integrality_matches(order: int = 24) -> bool:
+    """Check determinant parity, integral recursion, and the truncated equation."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(order)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    residual = sp.series(
+        f**2 - (p_zero / p_one) * f.subs(z, z**2), z, 0, order + 1
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(p_zero - p_one, z).all_coeffs()[-1] % 2 == 0,
+            all(coefficient.is_Integer for coefficient in coefficients),
+            sp.expand(residual) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def critical_zero_estimate_pullback_matches() -> bool:
+    """Check the cleared pullback identity and its two bidegree bounds."""
+    z, y = sp.symbols("z y")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    q = y**2 + z * y + z + 1
+    d = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(z)
+    n = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(y)
+    eta = max(sp.degree(p_zero, z), sp.degree(p_one, z))
+    pullback = sp.cancel(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: p_one * y**2 / p_zero}, simultaneous=True)
+    )
+    pullback = sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).as_expr()
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(18)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    evaluated_pullback = sp.series(pullback.subs(y, f), z, 0, 19).removeO()
+    expected = sp.series(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: f.subs(z, z**2)}, simultaneous=True),
+        z,
+        0,
+        19,
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(q, z, y).is_irreducible,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(y) <= 2 * n,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(z) <= 2 * d + eta * n,
+            sp.expand(evaluated_pullback - expected) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def rational_mahler_saturation_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify normalized saturation identities in exact rational examples."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    examples = (
+        ((1 - z) ** 2 * (1 + 2 * z) / ((1 - 3 * z) * (1 + z) ** 3), 2),
+        ((1 + z + z**2) / ((1 - 2 * z) ** 2 * (1 + 3 * z)), 3),
+        ((1 - 4 * z) * (1 + z) ** 2 / (1 + 2 * z**2), 5),
+    )
+    for rational_r, exponent in examples:
+        rational_r = sp.cancel(rational_r)
+        h = sp.cancel(rational_r.subs(z, z**2) / rational_r**2)
+        q = sp.cancel(rational_r**exponent)
+        delta_q = sp.cancel(q.subs(z, z**2) / q**2)
+        numerator, denominator = sp.fraction(q)
+        factor_exponents = [
+            multiplicity
+            for polynomial in (numerator, denominator)
+            for _factor, multiplicity in sp.factor_list(polynomial)[1]
+        ]
+        if not all(
+            (
+                rational_r.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                h.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                q.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                sp.cancel(h**exponent - delta_q) == 0,
+                all(multiplicity % exponent == 0 for multiplicity in factor_exponents),
+            )
+        ):
+            return False
+    return True
+

+Normal convergence of the logarithmic series on compact subdisks proves the
+analytic assertions and shifting the product proves
+\eqref{eq:critical-mahler-equation}.  The determinant congruence gives
+\(P_0\equiv P_1\pmod2\), hence
 \[
- B=\operatorname{diag}(c_1,\ldots,c_r),\qquad
- B'=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_r)
+ H(z)^{-1}\in1+2z\ZZ_2[[z]].
 \]
-are compatible sign blocks on this same base and satisfy
-\(\rad(B),\rad(B')\le a<\lambda\).  Their determinant ratio is
+Since
+\(F(z^2)/F(z)^2=H(z)^{-1}\), the Dieudonn\'e--Dwork criterion
+\cite[Theorem~1.1]{PomeratStraub2024RootsPowerSeries} gives
+\(F\in\ZZ_2[[z]]\).  Also \(F\in\QQ[[z]]\), directly from
+\eqref{eq:critical-mahler-product}.  For an odd prime \(p\), compare the
+coefficient of \(z^n\) in \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-equation}.  Its left-hand
+side is \(2f_n\) plus an expression in \(f_0,\ldots,f_{n-1}\), while its
+right-hand side belongs to \(\ZZ_p\) whenever the preceding coefficients do,
+because \(P_1(0)=1\).  Induction and \(2\in\ZZ_p^\times\) give
+\(F\in\ZZ_p[[z]]\) for every odd \(p\).  A rational number integral at every
+prime is an integer, proving the claim coefficientwise.
+\end{proof}
+
+The next estimate is not needed to reprove the special-value theorem below;
+it records an effective feature of the critical quadratic equation itself.
+
+\begin{lemma}[Critical quadratic zero estimate]
+\label{lem:critical-mahler-zero-estimate}
+Let \(P_0,P_1\in\CC[z]\) have constant term one, set
+\(\eta=\max\{\deg P_0,\deg P_1\}\), and let an analytic germ
+\(F(0)=1\) satisfy
+\[
+ P_1(z)F(z)^2=P_0(z)F(z^2).
+\]
+If \(F\) is transcendental over \(\CC(z)\), then every non-zero
+\(Q\in\CC[z,Y]\) with \(\deg_zQ\le D\) and \(\deg_YQ\le N\) satisfies
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-mahler-zero-bound}
+ \operatorname{ord}_{z=0}Q(z,F(z))
+ \le D+4DN+\eta N^2.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First take an irreducible factor \(q\in\CC[z,Y]\) of positive
+\(Y\)-degree and write \(d=\deg_zq\), \(n=\deg_Yq\).  Clear the denominator
+in its pullback by setting
+\[
+ \widetilde q(z,Y)=P_0(z)^n
+ q\!\left(z^2,\frac{P_1(z)}{P_0(z)}Y^2\right).
+\]
+This is a polynomial, with
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-pullback-orders}
+ \deg_Y\widetilde q=2n,qquad
+ \deg_z\widetilde q\le2d+\eta n,qquad
+ \operatorname{ord}_0\widetilde q(z,F(z))
+ =2\operatorname{ord}_0q(z,F(z)).
+\end{equation}
+We claim that \(q\nmid\widetilde q\).  Otherwise the irreducible curve
+\(C:q=0\) is invariant under the rational map
+\[
+ \Phi(z,Y)=\left(z^2,\frac{P_1(z)}{P_0(z)}Y^2\right).
+\]
+Pass to the normalization of \(C\).  The induced map permutes forward the
+finite set of places above \((0,1)\), so this finite dynamical system contains
+a periodic place.  Its Puiseux germ \(Y=G(z)\), based at \((0,1)\), therefore
+satisfies for some \(\ell\ge1\) the \(\ell\)-fold iterate of the same equation
+as \(F\).  Consequently \(U=G/F\) obeys
+\[
+ U(z^{2^\ell})=U(z)^{2^\ell},\qquad U(0)=1.
+\]
+If \(U=1+cz^\alpha+\cdots\), with \(c\ne0\) and the least positive Puiseux
+exponent \(\alpha\), the least non-constant exponents on the two sides are
+respectively \(2^\ell\alpha\) and \(\alpha\), a contradiction.  Thus
+\(U=1\), which would make \(F=G\) algebraic.  This proves the claim.
+
+Hence \(R_q(z)=\operatorname{Res}_Y(q,\widetilde q)\) is non-zero.  A
+B\'ezout identity in \(Y\), evaluated at \(Y=F(z)\), and
+\eqref{eq:critical-pullback-orders} imply
 \[
- \frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
- =\frac{\prod_i(1-c_i z)}{\prod_i(1-d_i z)}.
+ \operatorname{ord}_0q(z,F(z))
+ \le\operatorname{ord}_0R_q
+ \le\deg R_q
+ \le4dn+\eta n^2.
 \]
-Thus the omitted converse already contains multiplicative-relation questions
-for weighted products built from these linear factors; it is not an artifact
-of dropping the same-base compatibility or strict-gap hypotheses.
+Finally write \(Q=a(z)\prod_iq_i^{e_i}\), separating its polynomial content
+in \(z\).  The content contributes at most \(D\).  With multiplicities,
+\(\sum_i e_id_i\le D\) and \(\sum_i e_in_i\le N\); therefore
+\(\sum_i e_id_in_i\le DN\) and
+\(\sum_i e_in_i^2\le N^2\).  Summing the factor bounds proves
+\eqref{eq:critical-mahler-zero-bound}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Normalized saturation of rational coboundaries]
+\label{lem:rational-mahler-saturation}
+Let \(H,Q\in\QQ(z)^\times\) satisfy \(H(0)=Q(0)=1\).  If, for some
+integer \(m\ge1\),
+\[
+ H^m=\delta Q=\frac{Q(z^2)}{Q(z)^2},
+\]
+then there is an \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\), with \(R(0)=1\), such that
+\(H=\delta R\).
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For \(a\in\overline{\QQ}^\times\), let \(h(a)\) and \(q(a)\) denote the
+coefficients of \([a]\) in the divisors of \(H\) and \(Q\), respectively.
+Taking divisors gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:saturation-divisor-recurrence}
+ mh(a)=q(a^2)-2q(a),
+ \qquad q(a^2)\equiv2q(a)\pmod m.
+\end{equation}
+Fix \(a\ne0,\infty\).  For sufficiently large \(N\), among the
+\(2^N\)-th roots of \(a\) choose \(b_N\) outside the finite support of
+\(\operatorname{div}Q\).  Iterating the congruence along the chain from
+\(b_N\) to \(a\) gives \(q(a)\equiv2^Nq(b_N)\equiv0\pmod m\).
+The coefficient at zero is zero because \(Q(0)=1\), and the degree-zero
+condition on a principal divisor gives the same divisibility at infinity.
+Thus \(\operatorname{div}Q=mD\).
+
+The divisor \(D\) is Galois invariant and has degree zero.  Since
+\(\operatorname{Pic}^0(\mathbb P^1_{\QQ})=0\), choose
+\(S\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with \(\operatorname{div}S=D\), normalized by
+\(S(0)=1\).  Then \(Q/S^m\) is constant, and evaluation at zero gives
+\(Q=S^m\).  It follows that \((H/\delta S)^m=1\).  This rational function is
+constant and has value one at zero, so \(H=\delta S\); take \(R=S\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{proposition}[Algebraic critical products are rational coboundaries]
+\label{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}
+Let \(H\in\QQ(z)^\times\), \(H(0)=1\), and suppose that
+\(F\in1+z\QQ[[z]]\) is algebraic over \(\CC(z)\) and satisfies
+\(F(z)^2=H(z)F(z^2)\).  Then \(H=\delta R\) for a unique
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with \(R(0)=1\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put \(G=zF'/F\).  Logarithmic differentiation gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:log-derivative-mahler}
+ G(z)=G(z^2)+\frac z2\frac{H'(z)}{H(z)}.
+\end{equation}
+If the rational inhomogeneous term is non-zero, the equations at \(z\) and
+\(z^2\) eliminate it to give a homogeneous scalar (2)-Mahler equation for
+\(G\); if it is zero, \eqref{eq:log-derivative-mahler} and \(G(0)=0\) give
+\(G=0\).  Since algebraic functions are D-finite, B\'ezivin's theorem that a
+D-finite Mahler function is rational
+\cite[Theorem~1]{BellCoonsRowland2013MahlerDichotomy} yields
+\(G\in\CC(z)\), and its rational Taylor coefficients give
+\(G\in\QQ(z)\).
+
+All analytic branches of the algebraic function \(F\) have the same rational
+logarithmic derivative, so their pairwise quotients are constants.  Finite
+monodromy therefore gives an \(m\ge1\) for which
+\(T=F^m\) is single-valued, hence \(T\in\CC(z)^\times\).  Its Taylor
+coefficients give \(T\in\QQ(z)^\times\), and \(T(0)=1\).  Raising the
+functional equation to the (m)-th power gives
+\[
+ H^m=\frac{T(z)^2}{T(z^2)}=\delta(T^{-1}).
+\]
+Apply \Cref{lem:rational-mahler-saturation}, and then use the normalized
+injectivity proved in \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} for uniqueness.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Strict-gap determinant boundary lifting]
+\label{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting}
+Let \(A\) be a primitive non-negative integer matrix with Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\).  Let \(B,B'\) be integer matrices
+of the same size such that, entrywise,
+\[
+ \abs{B_{ij}},\abs{B'_{ij}}\le A_{ij},
+ \qquad B_{ij}\equiv B'_{ij}\equiv A_{ij}\pmod2,
+\]
+and suppose that \(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\).  Set
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}.
+\]
+Then the following are equivalent:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
+ \item \(\Pi_x(H)=1\);
+ \item there is a unique \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
+ \[
+  R(0)=R(x)=1,
+  \qquad H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2}.
+ \]
+\end{enumerate}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The strict gaps imply that both determinant polynomials are non-zero on a disk
+\(\abs z<r\) for some \(x<r<1\).  They are positive on \([0,x]\), because
+they are real, non-zero there, and equal one at zero.  Hence (H>0) on that
+interval.  Define (F) by \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-product}.  By
+\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}, it is analytic on \(\abs z<r\), has
+integer coefficients, and satisfies \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-equation}.
+Crucially, the product normalization is
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
+ F(x)^2=\Pi_x(H),
+\end{equation}
+not (F(x)=\Pi_x(H)).
+
+We apply Nishioka's special-value theorem
+\cite[Theorem, p.~387]{Nishioka1982MahlerFunctionValues} to the reduced form
+of
+\[
+ P_0(z)F(z^2)-P_1(z)F(z)^2=0.
+\]
+In her notation one may take (p=2), (N=0), (n=1), (m=2),
+(M=2), (U=1), and coefficient-growth exponent (L=1).  The required
+numerical inequality is (M(p+N)n^2=4<2^{2+1/L}=8).  The integer
+coefficients and analyticity of (F) give the required linear coefficient
+height bound, while the strict gaps ensure that the reduced coefficient
+polynomials do not vanish anywhere on the orbit (x,x^2,x^4,\ldots).
+Consequently, if (F) were transcendental over \(\CC(z)\), then (F(x))
+would be transcendental.
+
+Assume (i).  Positivity and \eqref{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
+give (F(x)=1), so the cited theorem forces (F) to be algebraic.  By
+\Cref{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}, (H=\delta R) for the unique
+normalized rational (R).  Now
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} gives
+(1=\Pi_x(H)=R(x)^{-2}) and (R(x)>0), hence (R(x)=1).  This proves (ii).
+Conversely, (ii) and \eqref{eq:rational-mahler-telescope} give (i), and the
+same proposition gives uniqueness.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Scope of the lifting theorem]
+The determinant parity in \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} is essential
+to the integrality step, so the theorem does not assert the converse for an
+arbitrary positive rational (H).  Its realizable class is nevertheless broad.
+Fix (r\ge2), an odd (a>0), and a positive even (b), and let (A) have
+diagonal entries (a) and off-diagonal entries (b).  Then
+\(\lambda=a+(r-1)b\).  Any diagonal (B=\operatorname{diag}(c_i)) and
+(B'=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)), with odd
+\(\abs{c_i},\abs{d_i}\le a\), satisfies the same-base compatibility and
+strict gaps, and realizes
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{\prod_i(1-c_i z)}{\prod_i(1-d_i z)}.
+\]
 \end{remark}
 
 This mechanism is strictly weaker than full \(G\)-cospectrality, equivalently

+def critical_mahler_normalization_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify that the weighted product is F(x)^2, rather than F(x)."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    x = sp.Rational(1, 3)
+    h = (1 - z) / (1 + z)
+    f = 1 - z
+    symbolic = all(
+        (
+            sp.cancel(f**2 - h * f.subs(z, z**2)) == 0,
+            f.subs(z, x) == sp.Rational(2, 3),
+            f.subs(z, x) ** 2 == sp.Rational(4, 9),
+            f.subs(z, x) != f.subs(z, x) ** 2,
+        )
+    )
+    if not symbolic:
+        return False
+
+    with mp.workdps(80):
+        real_x = mp.mpf(1) / 3
+        logarithmic_product = mp.fsum(
+            mp.power(2, -nu)
+            * mp.log((1 - real_x ** (2**nu)) / (1 + real_x ** (2**nu)))
+            for nu in range(12)
+        )
+        product_value = mp.exp(logarithmic_product)
+        return (
+            abs(product_value - mp.mpf(4) / 9) < mp.mpf("1e-70")
+            and abs(product_value - (1 - real_x)) > mp.mpf("1e-2")
+        )
+
+
+def _critical_mahler_coefficients(order: int) -> tuple[sp.Integer, ...]:
+    """Solve F^2=((1-z)/(1-3z))F(z^2) coefficient by coefficient."""
+    h_coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)] + [
+        2 * sp.Integer(3) ** (degree - 1) for degree in range(1, order + 1)
+    ]
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+    for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+        known_square = sum(
+            coefficients[index] * coefficients[degree - index]
+            for index in range(1, degree)
+        )
+        right_hand_side = sum(
+            h_coefficients[degree - 2 * index] * coefficients[index]
+            for index in range(degree // 2 + 1)
+        )
+        coefficients.append(sp.simplify((right_hand_side - known_square) / 2))
+    return tuple(coefficients)
+
+
+def critical_mahler_integrality_matches(order: int = 24) -> bool:
+    """Check determinant parity, integral recursion, and the truncated equation."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(order)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    residual = sp.series(
+        f**2 - (p_zero / p_one) * f.subs(z, z**2), z, 0, order + 1
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(p_zero - p_one, z).all_coeffs()[-1] % 2 == 0,
+            all(coefficient.is_Integer for coefficient in coefficients),
+            sp.expand(residual) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def critical_zero_estimate_pullback_matches() -> bool:
+    """Check the cleared pullback identity and its two bidegree bounds."""
+    z, y = sp.symbols("z y")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    q = y**2 + z * y + z + 1
+    d = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(z)
+    n = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(y)
+    eta = max(sp.degree(p_zero, z), sp.degree(p_one, z))
+    pullback = sp.cancel(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: p_one * y**2 / p_zero}, simultaneous=True)
+    )
+    pullback = sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).as_expr()
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(18)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    evaluated_pullback = sp.series(pullback.subs(y, f), z, 0, 19).removeO()
+    expected = sp.series(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: f.subs(z, z**2)}, simultaneous=True),
+        z,
+        0,
+        19,
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(q, z, y).is_irreducible,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(y) <= 2 * n,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(z) <= 2 * d + eta * n,
+            sp.expand(evaluated_pullback - expected) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def rational_mahler_saturation_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify normalized saturation identities in exact rational examples."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    examples = (
+        ((1 - z) ** 2 * (1 + 2 * z) / ((1 - 3 * z) * (1 + z) ** 3), 2),
+        ((1 + z + z**2) / ((1 - 2 * z) ** 2 * (1 + 3 * z)), 3),
+        ((1 - 4 * z) * (1 + z) ** 2 / (1 + 2 * z**2), 5),
+    )
+    for rational_r, exponent in examples:
+        rational_r = sp.cancel(rational_r)
+        h = sp.cancel(rational_r.subs(z, z**2) / rational_r**2)
+        q = sp.cancel(rational_r**exponent)
+        delta_q = sp.cancel(q.subs(z, z**2) / q**2)
+        numerator, denominator = sp.fraction(q)
+        factor_exponents = [
+            multiplicity
+            for polynomial in (numerator, denominator)
+            for _factor, multiplicity in sp.factor_list(polynomial)[1]
+        ]
+        if not all(
+            (
+                rational_r.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                h.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                q.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                sp.cancel(h**exponent - delta_q) == 0,
+                all(multiplicity % exponent == 0 for multiplicity in factor_exponents),
+            )
+        ):
+            return False
+    return True

+\begin{lemma}[Critical quadratic zero estimate]
+\label{lem:critical-mahler-zero-estimate}
+Let \(P_0,P_1\in\CC[z]\) have constant term one, set
+\(\eta=\max\{\deg P_0,\deg P_1\}\), and let an analytic germ
+\(F(0)=1\) satisfy
+\[
+ P_1(z)F(z)^2=P_0(z)F(z^2).
+\]
+If \(F\) is transcendental over \(\CC(z)\), then every non-zero
+\(Q\in\CC[z,Y]\) with \(\deg_zQ\le D\) and \(\deg_YQ\le N\) satisfies
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-mahler-zero-bound}
+ \operatorname{ord}_{z=0}Q(z,F(z))
+ \le D+4DN+\eta N^2.
+\end{equation}
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First take an irreducible factor \(q\in\CC[z,Y]\) of positive
+\(Y\)-degree and write \(d=\deg_zq\), \(n=\deg_Yq\).  Clear the denominator
+in its pullback by setting
+\[
+ \widetilde q(z,Y)=P_0(z)^n
+ q\!\left(z^2,\frac{P_1(z)}{P_0(z)}Y^2\right).
+\]
+This is a polynomial, with
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-pullback-orders}
+ \deg_Y\widetilde q=2n,qquad
+ \deg_z\widetilde q\le2d+\eta n,qquad
+ \operatorname{ord}_0\widetilde q(z,F(z))
+ =2\operatorname{ord}_0q(z,F(z)).
+\end{equation}
+We claim that \(q\nmid\widetilde q\).  Otherwise the irreducible curve
+\(C:q=0\) is invariant under the rational map
+\[
+ \Phi(z,Y)=\left(z^2,\frac{P_1(z)}{P_0(z)}Y^2\right).
+\]
+Pass to the normalization of \(C\).  The induced map permutes forward the
+finite set of places above \((0,1)\), so this finite dynamical system contains
+a periodic place.  Its Puiseux germ \(Y=G(z)\), based at \((0,1)\), therefore
+satisfies for some \(\ell\ge1\) the \(\ell\)-fold iterate of the same equation
+as \(F\).  Consequently \(U=G/F\) obeys
+\[
+ U(z^{2^\ell})=U(z)^{2^\ell},\qquad U(0)=1.
+\]
+If \(U=1+cz^\alpha+\cdots\), with \(c\ne0\) and the least positive Puiseux
+exponent \(\alpha\), the least non-constant exponents on the two sides are
+respectively \(2^\ell\alpha\) and \(\alpha\), a contradiction.  Thus
+\(U=1\), which would make \(F=G\) algebraic.  This proves the claim.
+
+Hence \(R_q(z)=\operatorname{Res}_Y(q,\widetilde q)\) is non-zero.  A
+B\'ezout identity in \(Y\), evaluated at \(Y=F(z)\), and
+\eqref{eq:critical-pullback-orders} imply
 \[
- \frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
- =\frac{\prod_i(1-c_i z)}{\prod_i(1-d_i z)}.
+ \operatorname{ord}_0q(z,F(z))
+ \le\operatorname{ord}_0R_q
+ \le\deg R_q
+ \le4dn+\eta n^2.
 \]

+\begin{lemma}[Normalized saturation of rational coboundaries]
+\label{lem:rational-mahler-saturation}
+Let \(H,Q\in\QQ(z)^\times\) satisfy \(H(0)=Q(0)=1\).  If, for some
+integer \(m\ge1\),
+\[
+ H^m=\delta Q=\frac{Q(z^2)}{Q(z)^2},
+\]
+then there is an \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\), with \(R(0)=1\), such that
+\(H=\delta R\).
+\end{lemma}
+
+\begin{proof}
+For \(a\in\overline{\QQ}^\times\), let \(h(a)\) and \(q(a)\) denote the
+coefficients of \([a]\) in the divisors of \(H\) and \(Q\), respectively.
+Taking divisors gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:saturation-divisor-recurrence}
+ mh(a)=q(a^2)-2q(a),
+ \qquad q(a^2)\equiv2q(a)\pmod m.
+\end{equation}
+Fix \(a\ne0,\infty\).  For sufficiently large \(N\), among the
+\(2^N\)-th roots of \(a\) choose \(b_N\) outside the finite support of
+\(\operatorname{div}Q\).  Iterating the congruence along the chain from
+\(b_N\) to \(a\) gives \(q(a)\equiv2^Nq(b_N)\equiv0\pmod m\).
+The coefficient at zero is zero because \(Q(0)=1\), and the degree-zero
+condition on a principal divisor gives the same divisibility at infinity.
+Thus \(\operatorname{div}Q=mD\).
+
+The divisor \(D\) is Galois invariant and has degree zero.  Since
+\(\operatorname{Pic}^0(\mathbb P^1_{\QQ})=0\), choose
+\(S\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with \(\operatorname{div}S=D\), normalized by
+\(S(0)=1\).  Then \(Q/S^m\) is constant, and evaluation at zero gives
+\(Q=S^m\).  It follows that \((H/\delta S)^m=1\).  This rational function is
+constant and has value one at zero, so \(H=\delta S\); take \(R=S\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{proposition}[Algebraic critical products are rational coboundaries]
+\label{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}
+Let \(H\in\QQ(z)^\times\), \(H(0)=1\), and suppose that
+\(F\in1+z\QQ[[z]]\) is algebraic over \(\CC(z)\) and satisfies
+\(F(z)^2=H(z)F(z^2)\).  Then \(H=\delta R\) for a unique
+\(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with \(R(0)=1\).
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put \(G=zF'/F\).  Logarithmic differentiation gives
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:log-derivative-mahler}
+ G(z)=G(z^2)+\frac z2\frac{H'(z)}{H(z)}.
+\end{equation}
+If the rational inhomogeneous term is non-zero, the equations at \(z\) and
+\(z^2\) eliminate it to give a homogeneous scalar (2)-Mahler equation for
+\(G\); if it is zero, \eqref{eq:log-derivative-mahler} and \(G(0)=0\) give
+\(G=0\).  Since algebraic functions are D-finite, B\'ezivin's theorem that a
+D-finite Mahler function is rational
+\cite[Theorem~1]{BellCoonsRowland2013MahlerDichotomy} yields
+\(G\in\CC(z)\), and its rational Taylor coefficients give
+\(G\in\QQ(z)\).
+
+All analytic branches of the algebraic function \(F\) have the same rational
+logarithmic derivative, so their pairwise quotients are constants.  Finite
+monodromy therefore gives an \(m\ge1\) for which
+\(T=F^m\) is single-valued, hence \(T\in\CC(z)^\times\).  Its Taylor
+coefficients give \(T\in\QQ(z)^\times\), and \(T(0)=1\).  Raising the
+functional equation to the (m)-th power gives
+\[
+ H^m=\frac{T(z)^2}{T(z^2)}=\delta(T^{-1}).
+\]
+Apply \Cref{lem:rational-mahler-saturation}, and then use the normalized
+injectivity proved in \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} for uniqueness.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Strict-gap determinant boundary lifting]
+\label{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting}
+Let \(A\) be a primitive non-negative integer matrix with Perron root
+\(\lambda>1\), and put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\).  Let \(B,B'\) be integer matrices
+of the same size such that, entrywise,
+\[
+ \abs{B_{ij}},\abs{B'_{ij}}\le A_{ij},
+ \qquad B_{ij}\equiv B'_{ij}\equiv A_{ij}\pmod2,
+\]
+and suppose that \(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\).  Set
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}.
+\]
+Then the following are equivalent:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
+ \item \(\Pi_x(H)=1\);
+ \item there is a unique \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
+ \[
+  R(0)=R(x)=1,
+  \qquad H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2}.
+ \]
+\end{enumerate}
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The strict gaps imply that both determinant polynomials are non-zero on a disk
+\(\abs z<r\) for some \(x<r<1\).  They are positive on \([0,x]\), because
+they are real, non-zero there, and equal one at zero.  Hence (H>0) on that
+interval.  Define (F) by \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-product}.  By
+\Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}, it is analytic on \(\abs z<r\), has
+integer coefficients, and satisfies \eqref{eq:critical-mahler-equation}.
+Crucially, the product normalization is
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
+ F(x)^2=\Pi_x(H),
+\end{equation}
+not (F(x)=\Pi_x(H)).
+
+We apply Nishioka's special-value theorem
+\cite[Theorem, p.~387]{Nishioka1982MahlerFunctionValues} to the reduced form
+of
+\[
+ P_0(z)F(z^2)-P_1(z)F(z)^2=0.
+\]
+In her notation one may take (p=2), (N=0), (n=1), (m=2),
+(M=2), (U=1), and coefficient-growth exponent (L=1).  The required
+numerical inequality is (M(p+N)n^2=4<2^{2+1/L}=8).  The integer
+coefficients and analyticity of (F) give the required linear coefficient
+height bound, while the strict gaps ensure that the reduced coefficient
+polynomials do not vanish anywhere on the orbit (x,x^2,x^4,\ldots).
+Consequently, if (F) were transcendental over \(\CC(z)\), then (F(x))
+would be transcendental.
+
+Assume (i).  Positivity and \eqref{eq:critical-product-square-normalization}
+give (F(x)=1), so the cited theorem forces (F) to be algebraic.  By
+\Cref{prop:algebraic-mahler-coboundary}, (H=\delta R) for the unique
+normalized rational (R).  Now
+\Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} gives
+(1=\Pi_x(H)=R(x)^{-2}) and (R(x)>0), hence (R(x)=1).  This proves (ii).
+Conversely, (ii) and \eqref{eq:rational-mahler-telescope} give (i), and the
+same proposition gives uniqueness.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[Scope of the lifting theorem]
+The determinant parity in \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} is essential
+to the integrality step, so the theorem does not assert the converse for an
+arbitrary positive rational (H).  Its realizable class is nevertheless broad.
+Fix (r\ge2), an odd (a>0), and a positive even (b), and let (A) have
+diagonal entries (a) and off-diagonal entries (b).  Then
+\(\lambda=a+(r-1)b\).  Any diagonal (B=\operatorname{diag}(c_i)) and
+(B'=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)), with odd
+\(\abs{c_i},\abs{d_i}\le a\), satisfies the same-base compatibility and
+strict gaps, and realizes
+\[
+ H(z)=\frac{\prod_i(1-c_i z)}{\prod_i(1-d_i z)}.
+\]
 \end{remark}

+def critical_mahler_normalization_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify that the weighted product is F(x)^2, rather than F(x)."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    x = sp.Rational(1, 3)
+    h = (1 - z) / (1 + z)
+    f = 1 - z
+    symbolic = all(
+        (
+            sp.cancel(f**2 - h * f.subs(z, z**2)) == 0,
+            f.subs(z, x) == sp.Rational(2, 3),
+            f.subs(z, x) ** 2 == sp.Rational(4, 9),
+            f.subs(z, x) != f.subs(z, x) ** 2,
+        )
+    )
+    if not symbolic:
+        return False
+
+    with mp.workdps(80):
+        real_x = mp.mpf(1) / 3
+        logarithmic_product = mp.fsum(
+            mp.power(2, -nu)
+            * mp.log((1 - real_x ** (2**nu)) / (1 + real_x ** (2**nu)))
+            for nu in range(12)
+        )
+        product_value = mp.exp(logarithmic_product)
+        return (
+            abs(product_value - mp.mpf(4) / 9) < mp.mpf("1e-70")
+            and abs(product_value - (1 - real_x)) > mp.mpf("1e-2")
+        )
+
+
+def _critical_mahler_coefficients(order: int) -> tuple[sp.Integer, ...]:
+    """Solve F^2=((1-z)/(1-3z))F(z^2) coefficient by coefficient."""
+    h_coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)] + [
+        2 * sp.Integer(3) ** (degree - 1) for degree in range(1, order + 1)
+    ]
+    coefficients = [sp.Integer(1)]
+    for degree in range(1, order + 1):
+        known_square = sum(
+            coefficients[index] * coefficients[degree - index]
+            for index in range(1, degree)
+        )
+        right_hand_side = sum(
+            h_coefficients[degree - 2 * index] * coefficients[index]
+            for index in range(degree // 2 + 1)
+        )
+        coefficients.append(sp.simplify((right_hand_side - known_square) / 2))
+    return tuple(coefficients)
+
+
+def critical_mahler_integrality_matches(order: int = 24) -> bool:
+    """Check determinant parity, integral recursion, and the truncated equation."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(order)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    residual = sp.series(
+        f**2 - (p_zero / p_one) * f.subs(z, z**2), z, 0, order + 1
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(p_zero - p_one, z).all_coeffs()[-1] % 2 == 0,
+            all(coefficient.is_Integer for coefficient in coefficients),
+            sp.expand(residual) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def critical_zero_estimate_pullback_matches() -> bool:
+    """Check the cleared pullback identity and its two bidegree bounds."""
+    z, y = sp.symbols("z y")
+    p_zero = 1 - z
+    p_one = 1 - 3 * z
+    q = y**2 + z * y + z + 1
+    d = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(z)
+    n = sp.Poly(q, z, y).degree(y)
+    eta = max(sp.degree(p_zero, z), sp.degree(p_one, z))
+    pullback = sp.cancel(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: p_one * y**2 / p_zero}, simultaneous=True)
+    )
+    pullback = sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).as_expr()
+    coefficients = _critical_mahler_coefficients(18)
+    f = sum(coefficient * z**degree for degree, coefficient in enumerate(coefficients))
+    evaluated_pullback = sp.series(pullback.subs(y, f), z, 0, 19).removeO()
+    expected = sp.series(
+        p_zero**n * q.subs({z: z**2, y: f.subs(z, z**2)}, simultaneous=True),
+        z,
+        0,
+        19,
+    ).removeO()
+    return all(
+        (
+            sp.Poly(q, z, y).is_irreducible,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(y) <= 2 * n,
+            sp.Poly(pullback, z, y).degree(z) <= 2 * d + eta * n,
+            sp.expand(evaluated_pullback - expected) == 0,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def rational_mahler_saturation_matches() -> bool:
+    """Verify normalized saturation identities in exact rational examples."""
+    z = sp.Symbol("z")
+    examples = (
+        ((1 - z) ** 2 * (1 + 2 * z) / ((1 - 3 * z) * (1 + z) ** 3), 2),
+        ((1 + z + z**2) / ((1 - 2 * z) ** 2 * (1 + 3 * z)), 3),
+        ((1 - 4 * z) * (1 + z) ** 2 / (1 + 2 * z**2), 5),
+    )
+    for rational_r, exponent in examples:
+        rational_r = sp.cancel(rational_r)
+        h = sp.cancel(rational_r.subs(z, z**2) / rational_r**2)
+        q = sp.cancel(rational_r**exponent)
+        delta_q = sp.cancel(q.subs(z, z**2) / q**2)
+        numerator, denominator = sp.fraction(q)
+        factor_exponents = [
+            multiplicity
+            for polynomial in (numerator, denominator)
+            for _factor, multiplicity in sp.factor_list(polynomial)[1]
+        ]
+        if not all(
+            (
+                rational_r.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                h.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                q.subs(z, 0) == 1,
+                sp.cancel(h**exponent - delta_q) == 0,
+                all(multiplicity % exponent == 0 for multiplicity in factor_exponents),
+            )
+        ):
+            return False
+    return True
+

+\begin{lemma}[Critical quadratic zero estimate]
